etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Ancient Greek ῥυθμικός (rhuthmikós), from ῥυθμός (rhuthmós, “measured flow or movement, symmetry, rhythm”) +‎ -ικός (-ikós, suffix forming adjectives), equivalent to rhythm +‎ -ic.

quote.citation: 2017, Velvel Pasternak, Behind the Music, Stories, Anecdotes, Articles and Reflections, page 226:
quote.text: The Beshtian School, faithful to this concept of song, was characterized primarily by happy-sounding and rhythmic melodies.

definitions.definition: Written in verse, especially rhyming verse.
With regular, repetitive motion or sound.
